bottom_line: In high-risk patients after myocardial infarction, valsartan vs captopril had similar all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 1.00; 97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.90 to 1.11).
implications: Based on the reported all-cause mortality hazard ratio for valsartan vs captopril (1.00; 97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.90 to 1.11) and the prespecified noninferiority finding (P=0.004), the results support concluding that valsartan was no less effective than captopril for mortality in this trial population; the reported death counts (979, 958) indicate similar absolute mortality. The combination arm does not support improved survival versus captopril (hazard ratio 0.98; 97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.89 to 1.09) and is associated with more drug-related adverse events.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind trial across many international centers comparing valsartan, captopril, or both after acute MI complicated by HF/LV dysfunction.
major_points.quote: We conducted a randomized, double-blind trial at 931 centers in 24 countries.

major_points.text: Patients were randomized 0.5 to 10 days after acute myocardial infarction to valsartan, valsartan plus captopril, or captopril.
major_points.quote: Patients receiving conventional therapy were randomly assigned, 0.5 to 10 days after acute myocardial infarction, to additional therapy with valsartan (4909 patients), valsar- tan plus captopril (4885 patients), or captopril (4909 patients).

major_points.text: Primary end point was death from any cause.
major_points.quote: The primary end point was death from any cause.

major_points.text: All-cause mortality did not differ among groups; hazard ratio for valsartan vs captopril was 1.00 (97.5% CI, 0.90 to 1.11).
major_points.quote: The hazard ratio for death in the val- sartan group as compared with the captopril group was 1.00 (97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.90 to 1.11; P=0.98)

major_points.text: Valsartan was noninferior to captopril for mortality within the prespecified margin.
major_points.quote: The upper limit of the one-sided 97.5 percent con- fidence interval for the comparison of the valsartan group with the captopril group was within the prespecified margin for noninferiority with regard to mortality (P=0.004)

major_points.text: Combination therapy (valsartan plus captopril) increased adverse events without improving survival.
major_points.quote: Combining valsartan with captopril increased the rate of adverse events without improving survival.

absolute_effects.quote: A to- tal of 979 patients in the valsartan group (19.9 per- cent) died, as did 941 in the valsartan-and-captopril group (19.3 percent) and 958 in the captopril group (19.5 percent).

subgroups.text: Prespecified subgroup analyses showed no heterogeneity in treatment effects on death or the secondary composite end point.
subgroups.quote: The examination of prespecified subgroups showed no heterogeneity in the effects of treatment on the risk of death or on the secondary composite cardio- vascular end point

harms.text: Combination group had the most drug-related adverse events.
harms.quote: The valsartan-and-captopril group had the most drug-related adverse events.

harms.text: With monotherapy, hypotension and renal dysfunction were more common in the valsartan group; cough, rash, taste disturbance more common in captopril group.
harms.quote: With monotherapy, hypotension and renal dysfunction were more common in the val- sartan group, and cough, rash, and taste disturbance were more common in the capto- pril group.

harms.text: Proportion no longer taking study medication at one year differed across groups.
harms.quote: The proportion of patients who were no longer tak- ing the study medication at one year was 15.3 per- cent in the valsartan group, 19.0 percent in the val- sartan-and-captopril group, and 16.8 percent in the captopril group

harms.text: Any adverse event leading to permanent discontinuation occurred in 282 (5.8), 438 (9.0), and 375 (7.7).
Angioedema leading to discontinuation was infrequent and no cases requiring intubation were reported.
harms.quote: Angio- edema leading to discontinuation was infrequent, occurring in 34 patients (0.23 percent), and the rate did not differ significantly among groups. No cases requiring intubation were reported.
